text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Friday April 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government has said it will not budge an inch to re-open negotiations with the striking Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) unless the workers accept the pay increase they were offered and return to work.
- A man suspected to have killed his wife and son through witchcraft was buried alive early this week and police found him dead when they exhumed him, police said on Thursday.
- Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) is contemplating discharging its legal advisor Viva Nyimba, accusing him of disorganising the union's solidarity in the ongoing strike by the civil servants.

- The government controlled Malawi Broadcasting Corporation (MBC) radio may transform into an organisation that would benefit all Malawians should the seminar on the review of the MBC Act set for this week-end prove successful.

- Tobacco prices tumbled to as low as $1.05 per kg at the Auction Floors early this week in Blantyre and forced sales to be halted till government officials, buyers and growers settled for reasonable prices.

- Doctors and nurses at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, the country's biggest hospital in Blantyre, on Thursday were contemplating to abandon the wards because police annoyed them on Wednesday by disrupting their union meeting.
- Striking civil servants union leader Thomas Banda said on Thursday the workers had "fired" their lawyer Viva Nyimba for airing anti-union statements on the local radio on Wednesday.
- The Ministry of Health and Population on Thursday confirmed that some of its hospitals were distributing expired quinine drugs to patients for treating malaria.
